document.title_main: - Business Requirements Specification for Jaywan Domestic and Co-badged Card Implementation
document.program: - Jaywan Domestic Card Scheme Enablement for Licensed Financial Institutions
document.type: - Business Requirement Specification (BRS) – Cards, Switching and e-Payments
document.overview:
- This document shall define the business requirements for implementing the CBUAE-mandated Jaywan domestic card scheme, including mono-badge and co-badged card propositions across issuing and acquiring for licensed financial institutions in the UAE
- The requirements shall ensure alignment with CBUAE circulars, Al Etihad Payments (AEP) guidelines and Jaywan scheme rules for domestic transactions, international routing, tokenization and digital wallets
- The scope shall cover end-to-end card lifecycle processes, routing configuration for domestic versus international usage, and integration with CBUAE / AEP infrastructures including the domestic card switch and dual messaging platforms
- The document shall reflect the objective of strengthening financial sovereignty, reducing domestic payment costs and enabling secure, seamless digital payments in alignment with UAE’s national payment strategy
document.current_constraint:
- Detailed CBUAE circular text and full Jaywan scheme rulebook are not provided in the input and shall be treated as external reference documents
- Technical specifications for AEP domestic switch, dual messaging, and tokenization frameworks are not available in this document and shall be obtained from AEP and CBUAE
- Exact service level targets, performance benchmarks and fee structures for Jaywan transactions are not specified in the provided content and shall be derived from scheme and bilateral agreements
- Final business processes for reversals, refunds and chargebacks under Jaywan are under discussion and shall be confirmed with AEP and CBUAE operations
- Detailed reconciliation formats and GL mapping structures are referenced as available with Finance and CBUAE but are not attached to the provided input
document.objective:
- The implementation shall comply with the CBUAE central government mandate that all licensed financial institutions shall launch Jaywan domestic cards as mono-badge and Jaywan co-badged cards with international schemes
- The implementation shall ensure that all new cards issued by banks currently issuing Visa or MasterCard shall in future be configured as co-badged cards that support both domestic and international transactions in line with CBUAE mandate reference number 5480-2024
- The implementation shall enable domestic card routing through the Jaywan / AEP domestic infrastructure for UAE and GCC-eligible transactions while allowing international transactions via partner international schemes for co-badged cards
- The implementation shall support reduction in domestic payment acceptance and processing costs while maintaining or improving service quality and security for cardholders and merchants
- The implementation shall ensure readiness of financial infrastructure, including card management systems, host systems, switching interfaces and reconciliation processes, to activate Jaywan locally and support future global expansion
- The implementation shall enable tokenized card usage via digital wallets such as Samsung Wallet at initial stage and support onboarding to Google Pay and Apple Pay as per AEP roadmap
- The implementation shall support CBUAE and AEP awareness and reporting expectations by enabling generation of required MIS, regulatory and reconciliation reports for Jaywan transactions
document.in_scope:
- Issuance of Jaywan mono-badge cards for domestic and GCC usage as per AEP and CBUAE guidelines
- Issuance of Jaywan co-badged cards in partnership with international schemes (e.g. Visa or MasterCard) for both domestic and international usage aligned with CBUAE circulars
- Configuration of card routing rules so that domestic transactions are processed via Jaywan scheme and international transactions via the relevant international scheme for co-badged cards
- Enablement of Jaywan card usage across ATM, POS, e-commerce and tokenized transaction channels subject to scheme and technical readiness
- Integration with CBUAE / AEP dual messaging system for e-commerce and tokenized transactions as a to-be process, extending from current Visa DMS arrangements
- Definition and documentation of end-to-end business processes for authorisation, clearing, settlement, reversals, refunds, chargebacks and dispute management for Jaywan transactions
- GL and reconciliation design for Jaywan domestic and co-badged transactions, leveraging existing GL structures validated by Finance
- Report definition and configuration for scheme, regulatory, operational and reconciliation reporting related to Jaywan
- Impact assessment and update of customer communications, product disclosures and fees for Jaywan card products
- Coordination and requirement gathering sessions (discovery sessions) for additional requirements for Jaywan mono-badge and co-badged cards with Business and IT stakeholders
document.out_of_scope:
- Definition of detailed Jaywan scheme technical specifications, which shall be governed by AEP and CBUAE technical documentation
- Commercial negotiations with international schemes or AEP regarding interchange, MDR, and fee structures
- Non-card payment instruments and non-card domestic schemes that are outside the Jaywan card initiative
- Detailed design and build of mobile wallet platforms (Samsung Wallet, Google Pay, Apple Pay) beyond business requirements for tokenization and usage enablement
- Customer marketing campaign content and creative design for Jaywan awareness activities
- Infrastructure capacity planning at AEP and CBUAE switch environments, which shall be managed by those entities

business_requirements.title_bs: - Compliance with CBUAE Mandate for Jaywan Co-badged Card Issuance
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall comply with the CBUAE central government mandate requiring all licensed financial institutions to launch Jaywan co-badged cards in line with mandate reference number 5480-2024
- The bank shall ensure that any bank currently issuing Visa or MasterCard products shall, for applicable portfolios, migrate new issuance to Jaywan co-badged cards that support both domestic and international transactions
- The bank shall ensure that card product configurations, customer journeys and operational processes reflect the dual-routing nature of co-badged cards
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- The bank currently issues international scheme-branded cards (e.g. Visa or MasterCard) without Jaywan domestic co-badging
- Domestic and international card transactions are routed exclusively via the respective international schemes based on current routing logic
- CBUAE mandate for Jaywan co-badging is not yet operationalised within card product catalogues, card management systems and processes
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall issue Jaywan co-badged cards where one badge is Jaywan for domestic usage and the other badge is an international scheme (e.g. Visa or MasterCard) for international usage
- The bank shall ensure that domestic transactions that fall under Jaywan rules shall be routed via Jaywan, while cross-border transactions shall route via the international scheme
- The bank shall update product governance, card application forms, customer communications and operational processes to reflect Jaywan co-badged status
- The bank shall align product rollout timelines with CBUAE circular implementation dates and AEP readiness
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Availability of official CBUAE circular including reference number 5480-2024 and related implementation timelines
- Availability of Jaywan co-badging rules and operating regulations from AEP and CBUAE
- Agreement with at least one international card scheme for co-badge configuration and routing
- Internal product approval from Product Committee, Risk, Compliance and Shariah (if applicable)
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall demonstrate that all newly issued eligible credit and debit cards are configured as Jaywan co-badged cards in line with CBUAE guidance
- The bank shall demonstrate that BIN tables and card ranges are registered and recognised by both Jaywan and the partner international scheme
- The bank shall demonstrate through test cases that domestic transactions route via Jaywan and international transactions route via the international scheme for co-badged cards
- The bank shall obtain documented sign-off from Compliance confirming adherence to CBUAE mandate requirements for Jaywan co-badged issuance
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- In case the international scheme co-badging agreement is not finalised for a specific portfolio by the mandated date, the bank shall seek clarification and potential phased implementation approval from CBUAE
- In case of technical constraints preventing immediate co-badge issuance for certain customer segments, the bank shall propose a migration roadmap and seek regulator concurrence
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- CBUAE circular and mandate reference number 5480-2024 for Jaywan co-badged card issuance
- AEP Jaywan scheme high-level announcement and readiness communication
- Bank internal product governance policy and card issuance standards

business_requirements.title_bs: - Issuance of Jaywan Mono-badge Domestic Cards
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall enable issuance of Jaywan mono-badge cards for domestic and GCC usage, in accordance with AEP scheme guidance
- The bank shall define customer segments and products where Jaywan mono-badge cards are appropriate (e.g. payroll, entry-level accounts, government programmes) in line with regulatory guidance
- The bank shall ensure that mono-badge cards transact only via Jaywan for domestic and eligible GCC transactions as per scheme rules
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- The bank does not currently issue Jaywan mono-badge domestic cards
- Domestic-only products may exist but are typically based on international scheme rails or proprietary local arrangements
- GCC usage for cards is currently routed via international schemes
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall configure Jaywan mono-badge card BINs and card ranges in the card management system for issuance
- The bank shall ensure that Jaywan mono-badge cards are accepted across domestic acceptance points enabled for Jaywan, including ATM, POS and relevant e-commerce, and as per AEP GCC arrangements when available
- The bank shall ensure that mono-badge cards shall decline transactions attempted outside the permitted domestic or GCC scope as per scheme rules
- The bank shall define fees, limits and features for Jaywan mono-badge products consistent with cost reduction objectives and customer needs
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Receipt of Jaywan mono-badge BINs and ranges from AEP
- Confirmation from AEP regarding GCC acceptance scope and rules
- System readiness in CMS, switch, authorisation host and ledger systems to support mono-badge products
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall successfully issue test and pilot Jaywan mono-badge cards and complete end-to-end transaction testing across ATM, POS and applicable e-commerce
- The bank shall validate that mono-badge cards are declined for non-permitted international usage according to configured rules
- The bank shall confirm that GL and reconciliation entries for Jaywan mono-badge flows are working as per Finance-approved design
- The bank shall have approved product documentation and customer disclosures specific to Jaywan mono-badge cards
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If GCC usage is not available at go-live, the bank shall configure mono-badge cards initially for UAE-only domestic usage and update configuration when AEP confirms GCC enablement
- If specific merchant categories are initially excluded, the bank shall document restrictions and plan phased enablement
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP communication on Jaywan mono-badge product options
- CBUAE payment strategy and policy documents on domestic schemes
- Bank internal product catalogue and card segmentation strategy

business_requirements.title_bs: - Domestic Versus International Transaction Routing Configuration
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall configure transaction routing logic such that domestic transactions for Jaywan mono-badge and the domestic leg of Jaywan co-badged cards are processed via the Jaywan scheme
- The bank shall configure routing so that international cross-border transactions for Jaywan co-badged cards are processed via the respective international scheme network
- The bank shall ensure routing configurations support cost optimisation, regulatory compliance and operational efficiency
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Routing logic currently directs all card transactions through international schemes for both domestic and international usage
- Domestic cost optimisation through a local scheme is not implemented
- Dual-badge routing rules and scheme prioritisation logic are not in place
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall implement BIN-level and country-level routing rules in the switch and host systems to prioritise Jaywan for domestic UAE transactions and applicable GCC scopes
- The bank shall implement logic in co-badged card processing so that terminal and routing identifiers enable correct selection between Jaywan and the international scheme
- The bank shall ensure that card-on-file, tokenized and e-commerce transactions follow the same routing principles based on location and scheme rules
- The bank shall ensure that routing tables are governed under change control with Compliance and Scheme Management approvals
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Clear routing rules and priority matrices from AEP and international schemes
- Switch system capability to perform multi-scheme routing based on BIN, MCC, merchant country and transaction attributes
- End-to-end testing environment to validate routing scenarios across ATM, POS and e-commerce
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall provide evidence through test cases that domestic transactions for Jaywan cards consistently route via Jaywan and not via the international scheme
- The bank shall provide evidence that international transactions for Jaywan co-badged cards route via the international scheme and not via Jaywan
- The bank shall demonstrate correct behaviour for edge cases such as GCC regional usage and cross-border e-commerce
- No revenue leakage or routing misconfiguration shall be observed in pilot or early life monitoring as per defined error thresholds
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- In case the Jaywan switch is temporarily unavailable, the bank shall define and agree with AEP on fallback rules, which may include controlled routing via international schemes where permitted by regulation
- In case of merchant acquirer constraints, transactions may temporarily route via international schemes with proper exception logging and reporting
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- AEP routing guidelines and interface specifications
- International scheme co-badging and routing rules
- Bank switch configuration standards and change management procedures

business_requirements.title_bs: - Enablement of Jaywan Transactions Across Channels (ATM, POS, E-commerce, Tokenization)
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall enable Jaywan card usage across ATM, POS and e-commerce channels in line with AEP readiness
- The bank shall include POS tokenized transactions within the Jaywan scope where supported by infrastructure and scheme rules
- The bank shall extend current Visa dual messaging system arrangements for e-commerce and tokenization to incorporate CBUAE DMS for Jaywan as a to-be process
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Current SMS process flows exist for ATM and POS transactions
- Current Visa DMS process exists for Visa e-commerce and tokenization transactions
- CBUAE DMS for e-commerce and tokenization transactions is documented as a to-be process but not yet fully implemented
- POS tokenized transactions are not explicitly handled under Jaywan
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall implement and document Jaywan transaction flows for ATM, POS, e-commerce and tokenized channels, including authorisation, clearing and settlement
- The bank shall onboard Jaywan cards to supported tokenization frameworks in alignment with AEP roadmap, including Samsung Wallet, and subsequently Google Pay and Apple Pay when available
- The bank shall ensure that POS tokenized transactions shall be processed under the Jaywan scheme for domestic usage where technically feasible and permitted by scheme rules
- The bank shall align message formats and process flows with CBUAE DMS requirements for Jaywan e-commerce and tokenized transactions
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Finalised process documentation for current SMS and Visa DMS flows as baselines
- Availability of CBUAE DMS specifications and Jaywan message formats
- Integration readiness with tokenization service providers and digital wallet operators
- Coordination and agreement with Card Operations, GBO-ATM/CDM and IT
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall complete end-to-end testing of Jaywan ATM, POS, e-commerce and POS tokenized transactions in pre-production environments
- The bank shall validate that authorisation, clearing, settlement and chargeback flows for Jaywan transactions are functioning as designed for each channel
- The bank shall demonstrate successful token provisioning and transaction authorisation in at least one live wallet (e.g. Samsung Wallet) at launch
- All relevant operational and support teams shall sign off on readiness for Jaywan multi-channel go-live
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If specific channels (e.g. e-commerce or POS tokenized) are not technically ready at initial go-live, the bank shall adopt a phased rollout with documented interim limitations and communicate clearly to stakeholders
- For unsupported wallets at launch (e.g. Google Pay, Apple Pay), the bank shall process Jaywan physical card transactions only and enable wallet usage as per AEP phased plan
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Current SMS process flows for ATM and POS
- Current Visa DMS documentation for e-commerce and tokenization
- CBUAE DMS to-be process documentation for Jaywan
- AEP communications on wallet enablement (Samsung Wallet, Google Pay, Apple Pay)

business_requirements.title_bs: - GL, Reconciliation and Reporting for Jaywan Transactions
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall implement GL structures and reconciliation processes to support Jaywan mono-badge and co-badged transactions in alignment with Finance-approved designs
- The bank shall implement regulatory and scheme reporting to CBUAE and AEP for Jaywan transaction activity, including cost, volumes and performance indicators
- The bank shall ensure that reconciliation processes are documented and align with CBUAE and AEP requirements
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- GL details for card transactions exist primarily for international scheme processing
- Finance has confirmed that GL details for Jaywan are available, but full operationalisation may still be pending
- Existing reconciliation processes and reports are primarily defined for current card schemes and CBUAE reports via Visa or other channels
- Original CBUAE reports have been shared with the bank, and documentation on reconciliation has been requested
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall configure new or updated GL accounts for Jaywan interchange, fees, settlement and chargebacks as per Finance instructions
- The bank shall implement automated reconciliation processes that match Jaywan authorisations, clearing files, settlement entries and GL postings on a daily basis
- The bank shall generate and submit all mandated CBUAE and AEP reports related to Jaywan volumes, values, disputes, failures and service levels
- The bank shall document end-to-end reconciliation workflows, exception handling and control points for Jaywan transactions
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Final confirmation from Finance on GL account structures for Jaywan
- Availability of CBUAE and AEP report formats and submission channels
- Availability of original regulatory report templates from CBUAE as reference
- Agreement on reconciliation responsibilities between Operations, Finance and IT
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall complete parallel run reconciliation for Jaywan transactions in test and pilot phases without material breaks beyond agreed tolerance
- The bank shall demonstrate generation of all required Jaywan regulatory and scheme reports in the agreed frequency and format
- Internal and external audit stakeholders shall confirm that controls around Jaywan GLs and reconciliations are adequate
- There shall be documented procedures for managing breaks, disputes and settlement mismatches specific to Jaywan
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If automated reconciliation for certain Jaywan flows is not feasible at go-live, the bank shall implement interim manual reconciliation controls with documented timelines to automate later
- If new regulatory report formats are introduced by CBUAE post go-live, the bank shall update reporting logic under formal change management
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Finance-confirmed GL design documents for Jaywan
- CBUAE regulatory report templates referencing Jaywan transaction data
- AEP settlement and reporting specifications
- Bank reconciliation and financial control policies

business_requirements.title_bs: - Disputes, Reversals, Refunds and Chargebacks for Jaywan
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall define and implement business processes for reversals, refunds, disputes and chargebacks for Jaywan transactions consistent with CBUAE and AEP rules
- The bank shall ensure operational clarity between domestic Jaywan dispute handling and international scheme dispute processes for co-badged cards
- The bank shall integrate Jaywan dispute handling into existing case management tools where possible
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Existing reversal, refund and chargeback processes are aligned with international scheme rules (e.g. Visa, MasterCard)
- Jaywan-specific dispute processes are under discussion, and updates on reversals, refunds and chargebacks have been flagged as required by stakeholders
- Operational teams are referencing current international scheme flows as baseline
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall document detailed domestic dispute flows under Jaywan, including timelines, evidence requirements and decisioning rules
- The bank shall configure dispute codes, statuses and workflows in internal systems to differentiate Jaywan domestic cases from international scheme cases for co-badged cards
- The bank shall train Operations and Contact Centre staff in Jaywan-specific dispute rules and customer communication requirements
- The bank shall ensure reporting of dispute statistics for Jaywan to CBUAE and AEP where required
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Availability of Jaywan dispute and chargeback rules from AEP and CBUAE
- Agreement between Business, Operations and IT on case management system changes
- Alignment with Legal and Compliance on customer terms and disclosures for Jaywan disputes
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall demonstrate at least one end-to-end simulated Jaywan dispute case from initiation to resolution in test environment
- The bank shall confirm that SLA tracking for Jaywan disputes is enabled and reported
- The bank shall confirm that customers receive clear and accurate communication templates for Jaywan dispute handling
- The bank shall ensure that dispute chargeback postings for Jaywan are correctly reflected in GL and reconciliations
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- Where Jaywan rules defer to international schemes for specific cross-border scenarios on co-badged cards, the bank shall follow international scheme processes while clearly classifying the case
- In absence of final Jaywan dispute rules at the time of implementation, the bank shall adopt interim internal policies approved by Compliance and updated once final scheme rules are available
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Existing dispute management SOPs for Visa and MasterCard
- AEP Jaywan rules on disputes, reversals and chargebacks (to be referenced when available)
- CBUAE consumer protection regulations relevant to card disputes

business_requirements.title_bs: - Discovery Sessions and Stakeholder Governance for Jaywan Requirements
business_requirements.description_bs:
- The bank shall conduct structured discovery sessions for additional requirements related to Jaywan mono-badged and Jaywan co-badged cards, involving Business, IT and Operations stakeholders
- The bank shall maintain minutes, open queries and decision logs including questions to be raised with AEP and CBUAE
- The bank shall ensure that outcomes of discovery sessions are translated into traceable business and system requirements
business_requirements.as_is_behaviour:
- Initial meetings have been held with attendees including Business Analysts, Managers and operational teams to review dual messaging processes and queries
- A meeting agenda exists covering process documentation review, VISA process clarification and how it can be adapted for JMB/JCB, questions to AEP and demand discussion
- Minutes of discussions with current progress and queries have been shared
- A table of discovery sessions for additional requirements for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged cards is referenced with meeting titles, dates and times
business_requirements.to_be_behaviour:
- The bank shall formally schedule and track discovery sessions for all impacted areas, including CMS, switch, digital channels, Finance, Operations and Compliance
- The bank shall document all business requirements, open questions and assumptions arising from these sessions in a controlled repository
- The bank shall ensure all queries to AEP and CBUAE are consolidated, tracked and responses incorporated into the requirements baseline
- The bank shall establish governance forums to review Jaywan implementation progress, risks and issues
business_requirements.pre_requisite:
- Availability of key stakeholders from Business, IT, Finance, Operations, Compliance and Scheme Management
- Agreement on meeting cadence, agenda and documentation standards
- Identification of a central coordinator or PMO for Jaywan programme
business_requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- The bank shall have a consolidated requirements register for Jaywan signed off by key stakeholders
- All high-priority queries to AEP and CBUAE shall have recorded responses and corresponding requirement updates
- Discovery sessions shall cover at minimum card issuance, routing, disputes, reconciliation, reporting and digital wallet enablement
- Governance decisions and risk mitigations for Jaywan shall be recorded and accessible for audit and regulatory review
business_requirements.alternate_flows:
- If specific stakeholders are unavailable for scheduled discovery sessions, the bank shall arrange focused workshops or bilateral sessions to capture their inputs
- If new requirements emerge after baseline sign-off due to regulatory updates, the bank shall manage these via defined change control procedures
business_requirements.reference_documents:
- Meeting minutes and agendas for prior Jaywan working sessions
- Discovery session schedule for additional requirements for Jaywan mono-badged and co-badged cards
- Bank project governance and PMO standards

non_functional_requirements.no_of_users: - To be confirmed based on bank’s cardholder base and target penetration for Jaywan mono and co-badged cards in coordination with Business and AEP
non_functional_requirements.peak_volume: - To be confirmed based on projected peak-day and peak-hour transaction volumes across ATM, POS, e-commerce and tokenized channels for Jaywan cards
non_functional_requirements.monthly_volume: - To be confirmed based on expected monthly domestic and international transaction counts and values for Jaywan mono and co-badged portfolios
non_functional_requirements.availability: - Systems supporting Jaywan transactions shall target high availability in line with CBUAE expectations for critical payment infrastructures, with specific uptime SLAs to be confirmed with Infrastructure and Risk functions

impact_on_operational_process:
- Operations shall update end-to-end card issuance processes to include Jaywan mono-badge and co-badged products, including KYC, card order, activation and reissuance
- Card Operations and GBO-ATM/CDM teams shall adopt the new dual-routing and dual-messaging flows for Jaywan domestic and international legs
- Contact Centre and Branch operations shall update scripts and procedures to handle Jaywan-related queries, including domestic routing explanations and dispute handling
- Reconciliation and Finance operations shall include Jaywan-specific GLs, settlement files and daily reconciliation activities in their standard run-books
- Dispute and chargeback teams shall manage separate flows, codes and timelines for Jaywan domestic disputes versus international scheme disputes on co-badged cards
- Reporting teams shall incorporate Jaywan metrics into operational MIS, regulatory submissions and management dashboards
- Operational risk and internal control frameworks shall be updated to include Jaywan transaction monitoring, exception handling and contingency procedures
regulatory_impact:
- The implementation shall comply with CBUAE circulars and mandates requiring domestic scheme adoption and co-badged card issuance
- The implementation shall support CBUAE’s objective of enhancing financial sovereignty, lowering domestic payment costs and strengthening the UAE’s role as a digital payments hub
- The bank shall ensure adherence to CBUAE consumer protection, data privacy and information security regulations in relation to Jaywan cards and transactions
- The bank shall align with any CBUAE and AEP guidelines on domestic routing, fee structures, dispute handling and reporting for Jaywan
- The bank shall maintain documentation and evidence for regulatory inspections demonstrating compliance with Jaywan-related mandates and circulars
- The bank shall ensure that cross-border bilateral arrangements (e.g. with India and other countries as per AEP roadmap) are implemented in line with CBUAE approvals and foreign regulatory obligations
reports_requirement:
- The bank shall generate regulatory reports to CBUAE capturing Jaywan transaction volumes, values, failures and service levels for ATM, POS, e-commerce and tokenized channels
- The bank shall generate scheme-level reports for AEP as required, including settlement summaries, chargeback statistics and operational incident logs
- The bank shall maintain internal MIS on Jaywan adoption, including number of cards issued, active cards, domestic versus international usage and cost metrics versus international schemes
- The bank shall generate reconciliation reports comparing Jaywan authorisation, clearing and settlement data with GL postings and bank side accounts
- The bank shall produce exception and break reports highlighting unmatched transactions, delayed settlements and disputes for Jaywan
- The bank shall leverage CBUAE-provided original report templates, adjusting internal data extraction logic to align with regulatory formats
access_requirement:
- Access to Jaywan-related systems and data shall be role-based and aligned with the bank’s information security and access governance policies
- Only authorised personnel in CMS, switch operations, Finance, reconciliation, dispute handling and reporting teams shall have access to Jaywan configuration and transactional data relevant to their roles
- Access to regulatory and scheme reports related to Jaywan shall be restricted to Compliance, Finance, senior management and authorised auditors
- Administrative access to routing tables, BIN configurations and GL mappings for Jaywan shall require multi-level approvals and be logged for audit
- Third-party access, including vendors and service providers supporting Jaywan integrations, shall be governed by contractual and security controls in line with CBUAE requirements
security_requirement:
- Jaywan cardholder data shall be protected in line with applicable PCI DSS standards and CBUAE information security regulations
- Tokenization shall be used for digital wallet and e-commerce use cases such that primary account numbers are not exposed to merchants or external parties
- Encryption shall be applied for Jaywan transaction messages in transit between the bank, AEP, international schemes and payment gateways
- Strong customer authentication and risk-based controls shall be applied for Jaywan e-commerce and tokenized transactions in alignment with CBUAE cyber and payment security frameworks
- Access to Jaywan configuration and transaction data shall be logged, monitored and subjected to periodic security reviews and audits
- Incident response procedures shall explicitly cover Jaywan-related security events, including potential data breaches, fraud patterns and system compromises
data_requirement:
- The bank shall capture and store Jaywan-specific transaction attributes, including scheme identifiers, routing choices, domestic versus international flags and wallet identifiers where applicable
- The bank shall maintain historical records of Jaywan transactions, disputes and settlements for periods mandated by CBUAE and internal retention policies
- Data models in CMS, data warehouse and reporting systems shall be extended to accommodate Jaywan product attributes for mono-badge and co-badged cards
- The bank shall ensure data quality controls for Jaywan BINs, card ranges, merchant category codes and country codes used in routing and reporting
- Data exchanged with CBUAE, AEP and international schemes for Jaywan shall be validated, reconciled and archived for auditability
- Any customer communications related to Jaywan cards and transactions shall be captured in CRM and archival systems as per regulatory record-keeping expectations
training_requirement:
